unit.title: Good people, or good situations?
unit.needIt: Whether you stop to help depends a great deal on whether you are in a hurry. Knowing that, you can arrange your days so your better self gets a chance.
unit.why: Aristotle says being a good person is like playing an instrument. You have to practice until it feels natural. But science shows that sometimes we don't choose our actions because of who we are, but because of how much of a rush we are in.
unit.outcome: Identify whether your actions come from your true character or just your current situation.
unit.reachesYou: You see this when you feel guilty for being lazy at home or when you feel like a hero for helping a stranger. It also shows up when you wonder if your friends are actually nice people or just acting nice for a reward.
unit.do: Notice one time this week when you do something good. Ask yourself if you did it because you wanted to be a good person or just because it was the easiest thing to do.

quiz.q: What is the third condition for a virtuous act?
quiz.why: The action must come from a stable character that lasts over time.
quiz.quote: And the third is that your choice isn't a one-off thing, which is happening in this situation but not in others.

quiz.q: Why does Aristotle say a person who acts justly by mistake isn't virtuous?
quiz.why: Virtue requires knowing that the action is virtuous.
quiz.quote: But because I was mistaken about who the brave ones were and who the cowardly ones were, I mistakenly imitated an action that turned out to be brave. Aristotle says, no credit.

quiz.q: What is the fourth condition Aristotle adds?
quiz.why: Aristotle believes a virtuous person finds pleasure in doing the right thing.
quiz.quote: The brave person on Aristotle's view is the person knowingly, for the sake of being brave, regularly, and with pleasure, acts as the brave person does.

quiz.q: What is the 'flow' state according to the lecture?
quiz.why: Flow is when you are so absorbed in a task that it feels effortless.
quiz.quote: And what he says, as you should know if you had the chance to watch his TED talk, is that it is when our attention is deliberately focused on what we are doing that the action is most experienced as effortless.

quiz.q: What does the Good Samaritan study show?
quiz.why: The study showed that being in a rush determined behavior more than the person's character.
quiz.quote: What was predictive of whether the seminarians stopped this man on the wayside was not whether they had prepared a story about the Good Samaritan. It was whether they were in a rush to get to their lecture.

partials: Virtue requires knowing the right act.
Virtue must be done for the right reason.
Virtue must come from a stable character.
Virtue should feel like a natural flow.
Virtue should be done with enjoyment.
crystal.key: Virtue is a stable character trait that makes doing the right thing feel natural and pleasurable.

decoys.text: Virtue is just doing the right thing.
decoys.why: Aristotle says it is not enough to just do the action; you must also be in the right state.

decoys.text: Character is the only thing that matters.
decoys.why: The lecture mentions that social psychology shows situation and circumstance often determine our actions.

crystal.aha: Virtue is when your character and your situation align so perfectly that doing the right thing feels like a natural flow.

beats.say: The one running late does not.
Aristotle wants steady virtue. Studies show the moment bends it.
